title: Xezar leader routing
description: Which lane the leader dispatches for each kind of work. A lane is a runner plus a model. This schema checks the shape only. The cross-references, the file-checked bans and the security minimums are checked by the kit's route script (`node .xezar/checks/route.mjs --check`), because JSON Schema cannot express them. Unknown keys are allowed so the format can grow; the route script ignores them and warns.

defaults.description: Which shipped defaults this file started from. `version` is raised only when the shipped defaults change; the upgrade diff compares against the stored copy of that version.

tools.description: Every runner a lane uses, keyed by the engine's runner ID.

lanes.description: Every lane, listed once, with its seven tags. Keyed by `<runner>/<model>`.

reservedLanes.description: Lanes kept out of ordinary orders. A reserved lane may appear only in the orders of the rows it lists. With escalation: true, the owner or the leader may also name it by hand on any row for unusually hard work, within that row's `never`.

checkedAt.description: file: the route check rejects the file. dispatch: the leader checks it when it starts a task. merge: checked before a PR merges.

noMatch.description: What the leader does when no row's trigger matches the work.

test.description: An example that settles a hard case.

text.description: Prose for the leader to read. At most 300 characters; the route check also refuses URLs and backticks in it.

laneId.description: `<runner>/<model>`; the model is the runner's own name for it and may itself contain a slash.

tier.description: very-strong: the most capable models, normally reserved (see reservedLanes). strong: trusted with judgement and verdicts. mid: everyday work with strong reasoning. cheap: bounded, procedural work.

loginId.description: An engine account ID. Committed, so never an email, a real name or a folder path. `default` is the engine's built-in login of every tool and is in no account file: under the leader's tool it is the leader's own login, and another tool may rotate on it.

rotation.description: Logins tried in this order when one runs out. Filled by setup from this machine's account list.

unlimitedLogins.description: Logins from the rotation that have no budget limit; the budget loop skips them.

lane.description: A lane. Every tag is required: a lane with a missing tag is rejected until it is tagged.

engineModel.description: The model name as the engine's list_models reports it, when it differs from `model`.

enabled.description: false switches the lane off everywhere. Default true.

match.description: A lane matches when every match key given here equals the lane's value. A row bans every lane that matches any one of its `never` entries. `why` is a note, never a match key.

writes.description: True when the task changes files on a branch.

runsCode.description: A row with writes: false whose step builds and runs the change. The tool-limits ban does not apply to it.

narrows.description: The broader row this one is a special case of. When both match, this row wins.

handledBy.description: The leader does this itself; no lane is dispatched.

lanes.description: Lanes in order of preference. The leader takes the first one that is available.

neverAuthor.description: The lane, login and vendor that wrote the work are banned; checked at dispatch.

neverClaimant.description: The lane that made the claim being verified is banned; checked at dispatch.

secondOpinion.description: Advisory lanes, each launched as its own task beside the chosen one. Its findings are never binding; an unavailable lane is dropped.

alsoDispatch.description: Other rows that are always dispatched with this one.

notes.description: Conditions that need judgement, for the leader to read.
